ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point \(C\) is a point on segment \(AB\), point \(M\) is the midpoint of segment \(AC\), and point \(N\) is the midpoint of segment \(BC\). If \(MN = 8 \, \text{cm}\), what is the length of \(AB\) in centimeters?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since point M is the midpoint of line segment AC, and point N is the midpoint of line segment BC, \\
$\therefore$ BC$=2$NC, AC$=2$MC, \\
Since MN$=$NC$+$MC$=8$cm, \\
$\therefore$ AB$=$BC$+$AC$=2$MN$=2\times 8=\boxed{16}$cm.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a horizontal line segment, with the endpoint on the left labeled B and the right labeled A; inside the line segment, from left to right, N, C, M can be seen in order. Reasoning: The problem gives that M is the midpoint of AC, so AC = 2CM; N is the midpoint of BC, so BC = 2NC.
